ledger.claim: The 'arrived' event at 18:15:10 was not an arrival, and the rider's complaint about it is made out on the platform's own trace. No admissible fix places the vehicle inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius at or before that timestamp: the first qualifying in-geofence fix is at 18:17:10, a derived dwell_start_offset_sec of -120.0 s, i.e. the app displayed an arrival two minutes before the vehicle entered the geofence. The driver_track's single stationary speed value (0.0 kph) belongs to the 22-fix in-geofence run that only begins at 18:17:10; every other speed value in the trace lies between 32.2 and 46.8 kph, all above POL-NS-05's 15 kph motion threshold. The driver also concedes the point in his own statement on the dispute record ('I pressed arrived a bit early'). Under POL-NS-05 the marker does not start the waiting clock, the clock runs from 18:17:10, and the false-arrival event must be recorded against the driver in the ruling's referrals. I do not claim this alone refunds the fee; the rider's submission on the money is the limb (b) point below.

The rider's account - that the app announced an arrival that had not happened - is corroborated by the driver's own message. At 18:15:30, twenty seconds after the 'I'm Here' tap and 100 seconds before the first admissible in-geofence fix at 18:17:10, the driver wrote 'im at the pickup point'. Read against the trace's own geofence test, that message asserted a presence at the pin that no admissible fix had yet established, and the rider read it at 18:16:00 while the vehicle was still outside the 50 m radius.

POL-NS-01 limb (b) is not made out on this record, so the fee is not chargeable. Limb (b)'s first branch requires a fix inside the pickup geofence at or before the 'arrived' event, and the trace contains none before 18:17:10. Its fallback branch opens only where POL-NS-05 finds the marker false, and that finding turns on two numbers - the driver's distance from the pin and his speed at 18:15:10 - neither of which this export supplies: driver_track reports only a minimum, mean and maximum distance across the whole trace, and no derived fact states the vehicle's position or speed at the marker. The party asserting that money is owed carries the burden of proving the facts that make it owed (POL-GEN-07(1)), and a charge is the exception while no charge is the default (POL-GEN-07(2)). The 4.50 carried on EV-FARE-02725 (payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00, cancellation_fee 4.50) is therefore not established on the record as supplied and should be returned to the rider.

Nothing external excuses the driver's absence from the geofence in the 120 seconds after he marked arrival. The traffic advisory artifact EV-ADVIS-02725-01 is MISSING for this trip - issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, weight_multiplier 0.0 - and its absence is itself citable: no KERB_RESTRICTION, ENFORCEMENT, CLOSURE or ACCIDENT covered Blk 108 Yishun Ring Rd in this window. With no advisory on the pickup road, holding position at the pin was lawfully possible throughout, and POL-NS-06(i) cannot be used to excuse or accumulate any part of the driver's time outside the radius.

Honest concession, so that the arithmetic is not in dispute between us: measured from the first qualifying in-geofence fix, the driver's continuous run is 210 seconds (22 consecutive qualifying fixes from 18:17:10 to 18:20:40), and the derived shortfall against the free waiting period is -30.0 seconds, i.e. a surplus of 30 seconds. The free waiting period in force for this trip is 180 seconds, read from trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec as POL-NS-01(c) directs. The rider therefore does not press a POL-NS-06 waiting-period shortfall, and does not put the 300 second figure in fee_schedule.minimum_dwell_sec in issue, because the resolution rule applies that figure only to records authored before policy version 2 and this record carries platform_policy.

In the alternative, if the judge cannot determine whether the arrival marker was false on this export, the record is one on which two admissible artifacts contradict each other directly on arrival and no clause resolves the conflict on the facts supplied: the trip_record's 'arrived' event states 18:15:10 while the gps_trace's first admissible in-geofence fix is 18:17:10, 120 seconds later, and POL-NS-05 can only bridge that gap by a distance and a speed at the marker timestamp that the export does not carry. That engages POL-NS-09(b), and the consequence is a human reviewer rather than an automated collection: the disputed 4.50 is placed on hold rather than collected or refunded. A fee that is held is a fee the rider has not paid, and on a record that cannot settle whether the displayed arrival was real, the charge should not be executed.

All four limbs of POL-NS-01 hold on this record. (a) The trip record carries a driver 'arrived' event at 18:15:10. (b) The trace places the driver inside the STANDARD arrival radius, the qualifying in-geofence run beginning at 18:17:10. (c) The driver then held position inside that radius for a continuous 210 seconds, exceeding the free waiting period in force for this trip - trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec is 180 and no_show_threshold_sec is null, so nothing longer applies. (d) He terminated the trip at 18:20:41 under reason code RIDER_NO_SHOW, with no boarding event recorded, one second after the 210 second dwell elapsed at 18:20:40. The cancellation fee is therefore legitimately chargeable under the anchor clause of this category.

The arrival geofence test of POL-NS-02 is satisfied, not failed. The trace contains 22 qualifying fixes inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius, each passing the 25 m accuracy filter - far more than the three consecutive in-radius fixes the clause requires - and the driver's minimum recorded distance from the pickup pin is 0.11 m. He was at the pin; the rider's assertion that he was 'still far away on the main road' is not what the driver's own trace, which the prepass grades COMPLETE at weight 1.0, shows at any point in the waiting window.

The effective in-geofence dwell exceeds the required minimum rather than falling short of it. The derived shortfall arithmetic returns -30 seconds against the 180 second STANDARD minimum, i.e. the driver waited 30 seconds longer than he had to before cancelling. POL-NS-06's full-refund route therefore cannot open on this record: that clause refunds only where the effective dwell is SHORTER than the free waiting period in force, and here it is longer.

The driver's own statement that he pressed 'arrived' a bit early is accepted, not disputed, and the derived arrival facts are consistent with it: dwell_start_offset_sec is -120, placing the 'arrived' tap 120 seconds before the first qualifying in-geofence fix from which the dwell runs. That costs him nothing. POL-NS-05(iii) provides in terms that where the corrected dwell nonetheless meets the minimum the false marker does not by itself defeat the fee and POL-NS-01 governs on the recomputed clock; the corrected dwell here is 210 seconds against a 180 second minimum, and limb (b) of POL-NS-01 is expressly readable from that first qualifying in-geofence fix. At most the early tap is a referral item for the ruling, not a reason to move the money.

Limb (d) of POL-NS-01 is satisfied on its own terms: the trip was terminated by the driver under reason code RIDER_NO_SHOW, one of the three codes that limb enumerates (RIDER_NO_SHOW, RIDER_UNREACHABLE, EXCESSIVE_WAIT). It was not terminated under DRIVER_UNABLE_TO_LOCATE, the only code the clause treats as the driver's own admission that he could not find the rider, and the branch to which POL-NS-01's sentence about in-radius stationary fixes and a full refund belongs. That sentence cannot be read as a general rule that a driver found inside the radius can never charge a no-show fee, because that reading would empty limb (c) of content and contradict POL-NS-06 and POL-NS-07.

The rider's own device places him nowhere near the pickup point for the whole episode. His track carries 70 fixes between 18:11:56 and 18:22:16, every one of them stationary (the only recorded speed is 0.0 kph) and 840 to 848 m from the pin, with zero qualifying fixes inside the 100 m rider-presence radius for this STANDARD zone. A rider who was waiting at the pin would not record a tight, motionless cluster more than eight hundred metres away, and the rider's account of the events is contradicted by his own trace.

POL-NS-04's exoneration route is closed at its very first limb. The chat log holds exactly one message and it was sent BY THE DRIVER, at 18:15:30 ('im at the pickup point'), read by the rider at 18:16:00; the rider sent nothing during the waiting window to locate himself or to ask where the driver was. There is no rider message that the driver left unanswered, in_app_calls is empty, and the driver then waited a further four minutes and forty-one seconds before cancelling rather than abandoning the pickup.

The charged amount is intact and there is no fare-integrity discount to be taken. The cancellation-fee line on the fare breakdown is SGD 4.50, which equals platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd for this trip and the fee_schedule default, so the line reconciles with fee_schedule.resolution_rule and no POL-NS-08(d) defect arises; the additional waiting-time line is 0.00 and no waiting fee is claimed on this trip, so POL-NS-10(d) is not in play. payment_status is CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd is 0.00 - nothing has been returned to the rider so far.

POL-NS-07 fixes the driver's payout once POL-NS-01 is satisfied and no clause from POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displaces it: 80 percent of the SGD 4.50 net fee, which the money block returns as driver_compensation 3.60. The anti-farming check does not trip, and it requires BOTH limbs: no_show_terminations_30d is 1, below the '4 or more' limb, and 1 divided by completed_trips_30d of 65 is 0.015, far below the 0.08 rate limb. The lifetime counters prior_no_show_flags and prior_deviation_flags are not the fields POL-NS-07 reads, may not be substituted for the trailing-30-day figures, and are not cited here.

ledger.claim: The outcome this record produces is DRIVER_COMPENSATION with amount_sgd mirroring driver_compensation_sgd at SGD 3.60 - the single exception POL-GEN-03 carves out - while the disposition of the fee itself is NO_ACTION, the rider's claim not being supported. On this rider-filed dispute that disposition is not a kindness to the rider: with payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00, leaving the present state as it is leaves the fee with the driver and returns nothing to the rider.

No escalation trigger under POL-NS-09 is present and the case is decidable on the merits. The counterparty-dispute counters are 0 on both profiles, so trigger (c) cannot fire; rider no_show_disputes_30d is 0 and the anti-farming check does not trip, so trigger (d) cannot fire; no two admissible artifacts contradict each other on arrival, dwell or rider presence, so trigger (b) cannot fire; and every artifact carrying a deciding fact here is COMPLETE at weight 1.0, so trigger (e) cannot fire. Holding the fee for a human reviewer would serve no purpose the record leaves open.

I rely on and disclose the absent advisory: EV-ADVIS-02725-01 is MISSING, carries weight_multiplier 0.0 and fires issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, and no advisory covers Blk 108 Yishun Ring Rd in this window. Its absence costs the driver nothing, because the 210 second dwell is already sufficient without any accumulation across intervals, and I do not assert the advisory against a MISSING artifact. The absence simply confirms that no limb of POL-NS-06 - including limb (i)'s summing of separate in-geofence intervals for a driver held off a no-stopping kerb - can be engaged here, and it is neutral as between the parties.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider and the driver: the SGD 4.50 no-show cancellation fee charged on trip TRP-02725 stands, and the driver is paid SGD 3.60. The rider is right about the arrival announcement, and that is the one point that goes against the driver. The trip record (EV-TRIP-02725) carries the driver's 'I'm Here' tap at 18:15:10, but the GPS trace (EV-GPS-02725, COMPLETE, weight_multiplier 1.0, 100.0% coverage, 10-second cadence, no gaps, 85 fixes) contains no fix inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius until 18:17:10 — a derived dwell_start_offset_sec of -120.0 s. The trace's only stationary stretch is the 210-second run from 18:17:10 to 18:20:40; every other fix is recorded at 32.2 to 46.8 km/h, so at 18:15:10 the vehicle was in motion and above POL-NS-05's 15 km/h threshold. The driver also concedes the point in his statement ('I pressed arrived a bit early but I did wait at the pin'). Under POL-NS-05 the marker is FALSE and does not start the waiting clock. What follows. The clock is recomputed under POL-NS-05 to run from the first qualifying in-geofence fix at 18:17:10. On that clock the driver held position at the pin for 210 seconds — 22 consecutive qualifying fixes, each inside the 50 m radius and inside the 25 m accuracy filter — against the free waiting period in force for this trip of 180 seconds (trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec; no_show_threshold_sec is null), a surplus of 30 seconds (derived shortfall_sec -30.0). The trip was then terminated by the driver at 18:20:41 under reason code RIDER_NO_SHOW with no boarding event, 31 seconds after the required dwell had elapsed. POL-NS-05(iii) therefore applies: the corrected dwell meets the minimum, the false marker does not by itself defeat the fee, and POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full on the recomputed clock. Nothing from POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displaces it: POL-NS-06 cannot open because there is no shortfall; POL-NS-03 has no application because the stationary fixes lie inside the 50 m radius, not outside it; POL-NS-04 cannot exonerate the rider because the chat log (EV-CHAT-02725) holds exactly one message and it was sent by the driver at 18:15:30, with no rider message and no in-app call; and POL-NS-10 is not engaged because the driver, not the rider, cancelled. The rider's arguments. The rider submits that POL-NS-01 limb (b) fails because no fix places the vehicle inside the geofence at or before the arrival tap, that limb (b)'s fallback branch needs a distance and a speed at the marker that the export does not carry, and that the burden of proving the charge therefore fails (POL-GEN-07(1)-(2)), so the SGD 4.50 should be returned. That is rejected. Limb (b)'s first branch does fail, but the fallback branch is the one that runs here: POL-NS-05's test is decidable from the record, because the trace shows a single stationary interval beginning only at 18:17:10 with every fix outside it at 32.2 km/h or more, and because the driver admits the early tap; the marker is false and limb (b) is read from the first qualifying in-geofence fix. POL-GEN-07 is not reached: clauses of the policy in force do license an outcome on these facts. The rider's alternative submission that this is an unresolvable arrival contradiction under POL-NS-09(b) is likewise rejected: the arrival tap and the trace are not two admissible artifacts contradicting each other with nothing to resolve them — POL-NS-05 is the clause that resolves exactly this gap, and it is why the fee survives. The rider's remaining points are accepted and made no difference to the money: the traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-02725-01 is MISSING at weight_multiplier 0.0 (issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT), so no KERB_RESTRICTION, ENFORCEMENT, CLOSURE or ACCIDENT covered the pickup road, POL-NS-06(i) cannot accumulate any time outside the radius, and the driver's 120 seconds outside the geofence are simply not counted; and the rider's concession of the 210-second run with a -30.0-second shortfall is the same arithmetic this ruling uses. The driver's arguments. The four limbs of POL-NS-01 are satisfied, but limb (b) only through POL-NS-05's recomputed clock, not at the arrival tap as the submission implies; the driver's assertion that the trace places him at the pin 'at any point in the waiting window' is right from 18:17:10 onward and wrong for the two minutes before it. POL-NS-02 is satisfied: there are 22 qualifying in-radius fixes, far more than the three consecutive fixes required, and the closest fix is 0.11 m from the pin. POL-NS-04 is closed at limb (a) as the driver says — the only chat message was his own — and the rider_track data (70 fixes, all stationary, 840 to 848 m from the pin, zero qualifying rider-presence fixes) is accepted as context but is not needed to decide the fee. The fare arithmetic is intact: the cancellation-fee line of SGD 4.50 equals platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd and the fee_schedule default, payment_status is CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd is 0.00, and the waiting-time line of SGD 0.00 is not claimed, so no POL-NS-08(d) defect and no POL-NS-10(d) issue arises. POL-NS-07 fixes the driver's payout at 80 percent of the SGD 4.50 net fee, which the money block returns as SGD 3.60, and the anti-farming check does not trip: driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 1, below the 4-or-more limb, and 1 divided by completed_trips_30d of 65 is 0.015, below the 0.08 rate limb. The lifetime counters prior_no_show_flags and prior_deviation_flags mentioned in that submission are context-only under POL-GEN-01, were flagged as such, and were not used as a ground of decision. No escalation trigger under POL-NS-09 is present: the counterparty-dispute counters are 0 on both profiles, rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d is 0, anti-farming does not trip, no two admissible artifacts contradict each other, and every artifact carrying a deciding fact is COMPLETE at weight 1.0. The money. The rider's claim is not supported, so the fee stands as it presently is (NO_ACTION as to the fee), and the outcome the case produces is DRIVER_COMPENSATION, with amount_sgd mirroring driver_compensation_sgd at SGD 3.60 as POL-GEN-03 requires. The monetary effect, SGD 3.60, does not exceed the SGD 8.00 execution threshold in POL-GEN-05, so it executes on issue. Confidence and weight. Every artifact carrying a deciding fact — EV-TRIP-02725, EV-GPS-02725, EV-FARE-02725 and EV-DPROF-02725 — is COMPLETE with weight_multiplier 1.0, so the POL-GEN-02(2) cap on confidence is 1.0. EV-ADVIS-02725-01 is MISSING at weight 0.0, carries no fact, and is disclosed by both sides as neutral. Confidence is set at 0.95, above the 0.70 floor in POL-NS-09. Referral. POL-NS-05(iii) directs that the false arrival be recorded against the driver so that the pattern is visible to POL-NS-07 and to human review; that referral is carried in this ruling.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
referrals: POL-NS-05(iii): record a false-arrival event against driver DRV-09725 for the 'I'm Here' tap on trip TRP-02725 at 2026-08-22T18:15:10 — no qualifying in-geofence fix exists before 18:17:10 (dwell_start_offset_sec -120.0 s) and the vehicle was in motion outside the 50 m pickup radius — so that the pattern is visible to POL-NS-07 and to human review.
